# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 20, 2026
**Member:** Cameron Foster
**Member ID:** W291434326
**Reference number:** POC-503C0E1587-87184
**Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), State of Nevada
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0287 – Hip Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/200_299/0287.html)

**Submitted to:** Aetna Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals), by fax to 859-425-3379 or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand this appeal must be received by **February 16, 2027**, which is 180 days from the date of the notice.

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which Aetna denied on August 20, 2026. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the plan's own published criteria in **Aetna CPB 0287 – Hip Arthroplasty** describe conservative care that my records show I completed. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I have set out the plan's criteria in its own words, followed by what is in my records.

## The conservative-therapy criterion the denial relies on

The plan's policy states:

> "History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year"

and:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication Footnote2 ** ), including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

My records establish the following:

- **Supervised, in-person physical therapy, 14 weeks.** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait from March 24, 2026 through June 30, 2026 — **24 visits completed** — documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That is 14 weeks of formal therapy, and it is entirely in-person supervised therapy, not home or virtual therapy.
- **My pain and loss of function continued despite finishing that plan of care.** I walk with a cane, I am limited to about one block, and I cannot put on my own shoes unassisted.

The policy also states:

> "Supervised physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy; ADLs diminished despite completing a plan of care)."

and:

> "Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

My physical therapy is confirmed by the actual PT discharge note, which was part of the prior authorization packet. If that note was not before the reviewer, I ask that it be obtained and reviewed before this appeal is decided.

I want to note one point about the length requirement. The policy's 24-week figure applies to "persons with a relative contraindication Footnote2 **," and that footnote is not reproduced in the criteria text available to me. My records document BMI 29, non-smoker, no active infection, and no untreated substance use. If Aetna applied a 24-week standard rather than the 12-week standard, I ask that the appeal response identify the specific relative contraindication it believes applies to me and where it appears in my chart.

## The other conservative measures the policy lists

The policy states:

> "Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises, and Activity modification; and"

My records establish:

- **Anti-inflammatory medication:** NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Flexibility and muscle strengthening:** my physical therapy was focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, over 24 visits.
- **Activity modification:** [please see my treating office notes regarding documented activity modification — my surgeon's office can supply these on request].

The policy also states:

> "Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote2 ** to joint replacement, optional for others); and"

My records establish that I ambulate with a cane.

And the policy states:

> "Therapeutic injections into the hip (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote2 ** to joint replacement, optional for others); or"

My records establish that I received a corticosteroid injection on May 5, 2026, which gave me only about two weeks of partial relief.

So even measures the policy treats as optional for members without a relative contraindication — an assistive device and a therapeutic injection — are both documented in my case, in addition to the medication and the supervised therapy.

## The remaining criteria in the policy are also met by my records

**Pain and functional disability.** The policy states:

> "Member has advanced joint disease demonstrated by: Pain and functional disability that interferes with activities of daily living (ADLs) from injury due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the hip joint; and"

My records document 18 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest, walking limited to one block with a cane, and an inability to put on my shoes without help. Putting on shoes and walking are basic daily activities.

**Physical examination.** The policy states:

> "Limited range of motion (ROM), antalgic gait, and pain in hip joint with passive ROM on physical examination"

My examination records document positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

**Imaging.** The policy states:

> "Radiographic evidence of either of the following: Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) with stage II or III disease; or Moderate/severe osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis of the hip joint (Tonnis grade 2 or 3; see Appendix for Tonnis grading scale); and"

My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph of June 13, 2026 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. The imaging report in my records does not assign a numbered Tonnis grade, and I am not in a position to assign one myself; the policy refers to an Appendix grading scale that I have not been given. I ask that the reviewer apply that Appendix to the findings actually reported in my radiograph, and that the appeal response state which grade was assigned and why.

## A note on what I have and have not been told

Some of the plan's criteria as published end in a colon and introduce further lists and footnotes that were not reproduced in the material available to me, and the policy also contains alternative pathways — for example, provisions addressing fracture, malunion, nonunion, malignancy, when conservative therapy is not appropriate, co-morbidity risk/benefit, and HbA1c for members with diabetes. I am not asserting that those alternative pathways apply to me. I am simply noting that I cannot see every criterion Aetna applied. **I ask Aetna to identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria from Aetna CPB 0287 – Hip Arthroplasty that my records were found not to meet, and what documentation would satisfy it.** Where I have argued a point in my own words above rather than quoting, that is because I have not been provided the plan's language on that point.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Aetna to:

1. Overturn the denial dated August 20, 2026 (reference POC-503C0E1587-87184) and authorize CPT 27130;
2. Review the complete record, including the physical therapy discharge note documenting 24 visits from March 24, 2026 to June 30, 2026, the June 13, 2026 radiograph report, the injection record from May 5, 2026, and Dr. Reyes's operative recommendation;
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with orthopedic surgery expertise; and
4. If the denial is upheld, provide the specific criterion relied on, the clinical rationale, the reviewer's credentials, and my further appeal rights, including any right to external review.

I have lived with this pain for 18 months and have done what was asked of me: months of medication, an injection, and 14 weeks of in-person physical therapy with a licensed therapist. I finished that course of care and I am still walking with a cane and unable to put on my own shoes. My surgeon has documented that surgery is now what I need. I am asking Aetna to apply its own published criteria to the records in front of it.

Thank you for your time and careful reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Foster**
Member ID: W291434326

Address: [street address]
[city, state ZIP]
Phone: [phone number]
Date: [date of signature]

**Enclosures:** [physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-06-30], [radiology report dated 2026-06-13], [injection record dated 2026-05-05], [letter of medical necessity from Reyes, MD], [copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-20]
